cases.sentence: ___ народа окружала освященную для свадьбы церковь.
cases.translation: A crowd of people surrounded the church prepared for the wedding.
cases.explain: «Толпа» is the subject of «окружала», so it is in the Nominative case.

cases.sentence: Полицейский офицер стоял у ___, сияя своим мундиром.
cases.translation: The police officer stood at the entrance, his uniform gleaming.
cases.explain: The preposition «у» ("at") governs the Genitive case: «у входа».

cases.sentence: Левин ходил взад и вперед по своему ___.
cases.translation: Levin paced back and forth in his hotel room.
cases.explain: The preposition «по» (movement along/around) governs the Dative case: «по номеру».

cases.sentence: Послали к Степану Аркадьевичу и привезли ___.
cases.translation: They sent for Stepan Arkadyevich and brought back a shirt.
cases.explain: «Рубашку» is the direct object of the transitive verb «привезли», hence Accusative.

cases.sentence: «Нет, как же!» — со сдержанным ___ говорил Левин.
cases.translation: 'No, how could this be!' Levin said with restrained fury.
cases.explain: The preposition «со» ("with", manner) governs the Instrumental case: «со бешенством».

cases.sentence: Священник, сам в лиловой ___, выходил к боковым дверям.
cases.translation: The priest himself, in a lilac cassock, kept coming out to the side doors.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» (describing what someone is wearing) takes the Prepositional case: «в рясе».

reading.ru: Толпа народа, в особенности женщин, окружала освященную для свадьбы церковь.
reading.question: Who crowded around the church prepared for the wedding?
options: A crowd of people, especially women
reading.correct: A crowd of people, especially women
reading.explain: The text says a crowd of people, especially women, surrounded the church consecrated for the wedding.

reading.ru: Полицейский офицер, пренебрегая морозом, стоял у входа, сияя своим мундиром.
reading.question: What was the police officer doing at the entrance?
options: Standing at the entrance, ignoring the cold, his uniform gleaming
reading.correct: Standing at the entrance, ignoring the cold, his uniform gleaming
reading.explain: The police officer stood at the entrance, disregarding the frost, his uniform gleaming.

reading.ru: Каждый раз, как раздавался писк отворяемой двери, говор в толпе затихал, и все оглядывались, ожидая видеть входящих жениха и невесту.
reading.question: What happened every time the door squeaked open?
options: The crowd's murmuring died down as everyone looked to see if the couple had arrived
reading.correct: The crowd's murmuring died down as everyone looked to see if the couple had arrived
reading.explain: Each time the door squeaked, the murmuring in the crowd died down as everyone looked, expecting to see the bride and groom enter.

reading.ru: Сначала полагали, что жених с невестой сию минуту приедут, не приписывая никакого значения этому запозданию.
reading.question: How did the guests initially react to the delay?
options: They assumed the couple would arrive any minute and thought nothing of it
reading.correct: They assumed the couple would arrive any minute and thought nothing of it
reading.explain: At first they supposed the bride and groom would arrive any minute, attaching no importance to the delay.

reading.ru: Священник беспрестанно высылал то дьячка, то дьякона узнать, не приехал ли жених, и сам в лиловой рясе и шитом поясе чаще и чаще выходил к боковым дверям, ожидая жениха.
reading.question: What did the priest keep doing as the groom failed to arrive?
options: Sending the sexton or deacon to check, and going to the side doors himself
reading.correct: Sending the sexton or deacon to check, and going to the side doors himself
reading.explain: The priest constantly sent the sexton or the deacon to find out if the groom had arrived, and went to the side doors himself.

reading.ru: Левин же, между тем в панталонах, но без жилета и фрака, ходил взад и вперед по своему номеру, беспрестанно высовываясь в дверь и оглядывая коридор.
reading.question: What was Levin doing in his hotel room, dressed only in trousers?
options: Pacing back and forth, constantly peering into the corridor
reading.correct: Pacing back and forth, constantly peering into the corridor
reading.explain: Levin, in trousers but without a vest or tailcoat, paced his room, constantly poking his head out into the corridor.

reading.ru: «Нет, как же!» — со сдержанным бешенством говорил Левин.
reading.question: In what emotional state did Levin speak about the missing shirt?
reading.explain: Levin spoke 'with restrained fury' about his situation.

reading.ru: «Рубашка на вас!» — с спокойной улыбкой ответил Кузьма.
reading.question: What did Kuzma say when Levin asked about his shirt?
options: That the shirt was already on him
That the shirt was lost forever
That he had forgotten to pack a shirt
That a new shirt was on the way
reading.correct: That the shirt was already on him
reading.explain: Kuzma answered with a calm smile, 'The shirt is on you!'

reading.ru: Послали к Степану Аркадьевичу, привезли рубашку.
reading.question: Whose shirt did they finally manage to borrow?
reading.explain: They sent to Stepan Arkadyevich and brought back a shirt.

reading.ru: Через три минуты, не глядя на часы, чтобы не растравлять раны, Левин бегом бежал по коридору.
reading.question: How did Levin finally head toward the church once the shirt arrived?
options: Running down the corridor, avoiding looking at the clock
reading.correct: Running down the corridor, avoiding looking at the clock
reading.explain: Three minutes later, not looking at the clock so as not to aggravate his anguish, Levin ran down the corridor.
